headline: New law requires FEMA to use one standard process to review certain anti-terrorism grant requests for first responder equipment.
what_it_does: This law directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to set up a uniform process for reviewing certain anti-terrorism grant applications. The process applies when a city area, state, local, or tribal government asks to use grant money to buy first responder equipment or systems that do not meet or exceed national voluntary consensus standards.

who_it_affects.how: Their anti-terrorism grant requests to buy equipment that does not meet national voluntary standards will be reviewed under one uniform FEMA process.
Their applications to buy first responder equipment or systems that fall outside national voluntary standards will go through the same FEMA review process.

who_it_affects.group: First responders such as police, firefighters, and emergency medical workers
who_it_affects.how: The equipment and systems their agencies can buy with these grants may be affected by how FEMA reviews requests for gear that does not meet national voluntary standards.
The agency must create and carry out a consistent review process for these grant applications.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; the summary does not give a specific start date for the review process.
